Synopsis:
Senate Democrats are pushing back against new USPS mail-in voting rules enacted under a Trump executive order ahead of November 2026 congressional elections. A federal judge has temporarily blocked enforcement. The administration is seeking Supreme Court intervention to reinstate the rules. Critics warn the regulations — requiring state voter lists and standardized ballot envelopes with barcodes — could collapse the absentee ballot system and disenfranchise millions. The political stakes are high as Republicans fight to retain Congressional control, with Democrats arguing the rules disproportionately suppress Democratic-leaning voters.
